dashboard.summary: The war came ashore in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait this week, and it cost lives. For our corridor, Singapore fuel is dearer but quicker to deliver.

bluf.title: Seven ships hit around Musandam
bluf.text: Seven ships were hit in three days, including three loaded VLCCs within 17 minutes on 22 November and a bulker at the Dibba anchorage. All crews were reported safe.

bluf.title: Lives lost ashore
bluf.text: A Houthi strike on the Jazan refinery killed a worker and halted some operations; two Italian technicians were killed by drone debris in Kuwait.

bluf.title: Oil rises for the first time in a month
bluf.text: Brent (January contract) rose about 7% to around US$97 as attacks reached Saudi refineries. It rolls to February on 30 November.

bluf.title: Singapore dearer but faster
bluf.text: VLSFO rose to US$861–895/mt, but lead times eased to 12–14 days and LSMGO to 5–8. December slots are already being booked.

dashboard.baseCase: Brent (February contract) trades US$88–100 next week. A hit on a Saudi export terminal or a direct US–Iran exchange could push it above US$100; a pause in attacks would let the surplus reassert itself.
dashboard.bunkerNote: Singapore ranges span ENGINE (12:00 SGT, 26 Nov) and Integr8 (early 27 Nov); Fujairah figures are Integr8 indications. Singapore lead times: VLSFO 12–14 days, LSMGO 5–8, HSFO ~10. Forward paper points lower: Singapore 0.5% falls from about US$747 to US$627 three months out (Integr8).
dashboard.incidentsNote: Attacks now land on both sides of the Musandam Peninsula and at UAE east-coast anchorages. Correction to Issue 017: the missing Jordanian officer was aboard the ADNOC-operated tanker hit on 17 November, which appears to be the same incident as the unnamed tanker 13 nm north of Khasab.
